setup.title: Finish setup
setup.intro: The app is running but isn't connected to a database yet. Three steps and you're ready.
setup.step1Body: Go to supabase.com, create a new project (the free plan is enough), and pick a European region.
setup.step2Body: Copy each file from supabase/migrations into the project's SQL editor and run them in order.
setup.step3Body: Copy .env.example to .env.local inside apps/web and apps/portal, then fill in the URL and anon key from Project Settings → API.
setup.restartNote: Restart the dev server after editing the environment files.
setup.readmeLink: The full walkthrough lives in the project README.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Clinic-wide preferences
settings.inventoryIntro: Do you keep herb stock at the clinic?

tracksOn.title: Yes, I hold stock
tracksOn.body: The stock room appears in the menu, and every herb and formula in the library shows what is on the shelf. Dispensing during a treatment deducts from it.

tracksOff.title: No, I only prescribe
tracksOff.body: Everything to do with stock disappears — the stock room, batches, suppliers and quantities. A treatment records what you prescribed without deducting anything.

settings.inventoryReversible: Change it whenever you like. Turning it off hides your stock data rather than deleting it, so turning it back on restores exactly what was there.

anomalies.title: Unusual patterns
anomalies.clearBody: No unusual access patterns in the last 30 days.
anomalies.rules: Two rules, deliberately blunt: thirty or more distinct records in one hour, or five or more reads between 23:00 and 06:00. A flag is not proof of anything — it is a reason to look. Failed logins and login location are not monitored yet: they live in the authentication layer rather than the database.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.subtitle: What is accessible, what is not yet, and who to contact
accessibility.intro: We treat accessibility as part of the craft rather than an addition to it. This system is built so that everyone working in the clinic can use it — with a mouse, with a keyboard alone, or with a screen reader.
accessibility.standard: The system is built to Israeli standard 5568, which follows WCAG 2.1 level AA. This statement is updated as the work continues.

done.keyboard: Full keyboard navigation on every screen — menus, filters, table sorting and the acupuncture point chart included — with a visible focus indicator throughout.
done.contrast: Every colour pair that carries text is measured automatically against the 4.5:1 requirement. The check runs on the built code and fails if a new pair falls below the threshold.
done.landmarks: Semantic HTML: a correct heading hierarchy, navigation, main content and header marked as such, and a skip-to-content link at the top of every page.
done.labels: Every form field has an associated label, and every error message is linked to its field and announced — not signalled by colour alone.
done.rtl: Full right-to-left Hebrew support, including menus, tables and dialogs mirroring correctly, while phone numbers and Latin codes keep their own direction.
done.zoom: The layout is built in relative units and stays usable at 200% text zoom.
done.motion: No flashing animation, nothing that moves on its own, and no time limit on completing a form.
done.automated: Automated checks run on every code change: contrast is measured from the stylesheet across 101 pairs, and axe checks labels, accessible names, heading order and direction.

accessibility.gapsIntro: This list is deliberately specific. A statement that claims full conformance and is wrong is worse than one that names its own limits.

gaps.screenReaderAudit: A full manual pass with a screen reader (NVDA or VoiceOver) has not been done yet. Fixes so far were driven by the code and by automated checks.
gaps.bodyMap: The acupuncture body chart is keyboard operable, but it is a schematic visual. The same information is fully available in the point list beside it.
gaps.calendar: The calendar view has not had a full accessibility pass. Every appointment is also reachable from the patient file.
gaps.pdf: Uploaded documents are shown as they arrive. If a document we receive is not accessible, we cannot make it so after the fact.
gaps.automatedScope: The automated axe check currently covers the public pages only. The screens behind the login need a test environment with synthetic data, which is not yet in place.

accessibility.contactBody: If something stops you using the system, we want to hear about it and will act on it. Accessibility reports are handled as a priority.
accessibility.placeholderWarning: The accessibility coordinator has not been named. Before this system serves patients, a name, email address and phone number must be entered here — a statement with no way to make contact does not meet the standard.

consent.title: Consent
consent.intro: Each consent records the exact version of the document the patient accepted, and when. Withdrawing is recorded as a new decision and does not erase the earlier one.
consent.noDocument: No document published for this kind yet
consent.exportBody: Downloads everything the clinic holds about this patient as one file: personal details, medical history, appointments, treatments, clinical notes, prescriptions, the document list, the consent history, and who accessed the record and when. Uploaded documents are listed by name and date; the files themselves are downloaded separately.
consent.documentsSubtitle: The texts patients are asked to accept
consent.immutableNote: A published document cannot be edited — that is what lets a consent from two years ago still say exactly what was agreed. To correct one, publish a new version; the old one is kept.
consent.bodyHint: The full text exactly as the patient will see it.
consent.tooShort: A title and a full text are both required.
consent.publishWarning: Once published the text cannot be edited. Make sure it is final — a correction means publishing a new version.
